articles.title_orig: CoreWeave Earnings Beat Expectations, Assuaging Market Nervousness
articles.title_zh: CoreWeave Earnings Beat Expectations, Assuaging Market Nervousness
articles.content_orig:
CoreWeave faces a pivotal test when it reports its third-quarter financial results after the bell on Tuesday.
The market will be closely watching what the neocloud company says about artificial intelligence spending — and how it plans to finance its infrastructure buildout. The outcome could either calm concerns over its debt or stoke more fear.
"Investors need neoclouds to quantify how much financing they expect to raise to execute on existing backlog," Wolfe Research said in a note Monday. "We think outlooks that communicate when and which avenues of funding will be tapped will increase investor confidence."
CoreWeave stock and bonds have come under pressure as fears deepened about the enormous amount of debt it has taken out to build its data centers.
Its stock is down roughly 40% over the past month. Meanwhile, the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 15.5% on Tuesday, after jumping to 16.7% on Thursday as investors digested the election results and possible roadblocks to data center construction. Bond yields move inversely to prices.
The spread on its five-year credit default swaps — which is insurance against default and considered a barometer of perceived credit risk — is also at levels that are considered distressed. On Tuesday, its CDS spread stood around 1,152 basis points, after rising above its October peak to close at 1,278 basis points on Thursday. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.
In addition, the New Jersey-based company's leverage is high. CoreWeave has a debt-to-equity ratio of 702%, up from almost 291% a year ago.
CEO Michael Intrator has sought to quell investor fear, posting on LinkedIn after the election last week that the company doesn't anticipate "any impact to CoreWeave's existing customer commitments or associated backlog as a result of shifts in the political landscape."
The company reported a revenue backlog of $104.2 billion in the second quarter . It has about $35 billion in debt, as of June 30.
CoreWeave has already given a picture of what it expects for the third quarter.
It guided for quarterly revenue of $3.4 billion to $3.6 billion when it reported second-quarter results in August. It anticipated capital expenditures between $11.5 billion and $13.5 billion for the quarter and $35 billion to $39 billion for the full year. The company also expects 1.85 gigawatts in active power by year-end.
Wells Fargo expects the company's capex needs for the rest of the year to be largely covered by its remaining undrawn debt, debt issuances in August/September and the $12 billion it is holding for project costs, which will flow into capex, analyst Michael Turrin said in a note Sunday.
However, its 2027 capex could reach $66 billion, based on an expected capacity addition of 1.5 gigawatts, Turrin said. That will require at least $25 billion more in debt, he noted. It can be largely funded through delayed draw term loans, which allows CoreWeave to draw down funds over time, and the rest can come through bonds and convertibles, he said.
Turrin has an overweight rating and $115 price target on the stock, implying 135% upside from Monday's close.
"While neoclouds sit in the eye of the AI storm, we remain confident that CRWV is the highest quality co in the space," Turrin wrote. "Beyond the noise, we see capacity/revs coming in better than expected (1.95GW this yr vs guide 1.85GW) as margins start to inflect."
However, investors likely won't get all the answers they're seeking during CoreWeave's third-quarter results, said CreditSights analyst Jordan Chalfin.
"One of the major issues for CoreWeave is whether or not they can obtain all the financing they need," he said. "They may try and calm the markets, but I'm not sure how much color they can and will provide."
Investors will be looking for 2027 guidance on capex and free cash flow, though that may not come until Coreweave releases fourth quarter results, Chalfin notes.
CoreWeave could ease investor concerns by showing it has plans and approvals in place to scale capacity through 2027, he said. The company can also demonstrate remaining performance obligation (RPO) growth, which shows the total value of its contracted future revenue, and highlight new customer wins.
In addition, pricing has been really strong on recent deals, Chalfin pointed out. "That could show up in an operating margin beat for Q3 and expectations for Q4."
While CoreWeave faces finances challenges, the company has many ways to access capital, Chalfin said. That includes chip-backed deals, which allow Corewave to borrow money using GPUs as collateral, and original equipment manufacturer financing. For instance, CoreWeave could turn to Dell , which is a big supplier with a strong balance sheet, Chalfin noted.
"Despite all the market sentiment, fundamentals are actually quite strong and pricing is strong," he said. "The trends over the next few quarters, I think, should be supportive." Risks could arise after that, but it is "too early to call."
Some analysts remain skeptical that Coreweave will be able to calm credit fears.
Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, points out that the company is facing a huge bill in just over two years. CoreWeave owes roughly $15 billion in principal payments through 2028, according to its second-quarter earnings statement .
"They don't have enough cash to service all that debt," he said. "Unless some big orders come in, unless some big money flows come in for them in the next 17, 18 months, I think this is going to be the start of the end for CoreWeave, unless somebody comes in and wants to buy them. But who wants to buy all that debt?"
However, there could be a "small" window for the company to push out its debt for another three to five years, but it will depend on how strong their cash flow is when they report on Tuesday, Lang said.
Plus, issuing equity to help fund infrastructure projects, like Meta and Oracle did recently , isn't an option for CoreWeave, he noted.
"They're going to dilute the stock so much that it's going to continue to go down," he said. "They missed that window when the stock was in the hundreds."
CoreWeave topped $183 in June 2025. It has since declined more than 73%, recently trading around $47.
Despite the fall, analysts remain bullish on the stock with an average overweight rating and $126 target, based on 39 estimates complied by FactSet.
—CNBC's Jordan Novet contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
articles.title_zh: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
articles.content_orig:
"He's suffering": Trump answers BBC question about Nvidia's Jensen Huang
US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy.
Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign.
"I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.
Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
Speaking later at a White House press briefing, Trump told reporters, "I know the FBI is looking into" the affair but did not give further details on the investigation, or confirm when it was launched.
Trump added he thought that Huang was an "honourable guy and I feel very confident that he will be in good shape" after the investigations.
The FBI declined to comment when contacted by the BBC.
Nvidia, which has commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.
Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company after Apple, and designs computer chips that have become central to AI technology.
The revelations knocked about $250bn (Â£190bn) off Nvidia's value on Monday as the company's share price fell by more than 4%.
US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang , also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. She is not related to Jensen Huang.
According to the newspaper, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington in spring this year, warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
Trump's remarks are the first indication of whether Nvidia's Huang knew about the woman's alleged ties to Chinese espionage.
Megaspeed's office in Singapore's central business district appeared to be operational and staffed on Tuesday.
The BBC was refused entry to its floor, but spoke to a staff member by phone who said they had no comment and directed all queries to the company's PR team.
The BBC has emailed Megaspeed several times for comment.
Nvidia, co-founded by Jensen Huang, is also a major focus in the AI technology race between the US and China, with officials in Washington treating its exports to Beijing as a matter of national security - a key reason why Huang's affair has sparked concerns.
Also on Monday, Huang and Nvidia were sued in a proposed class action lawsuit in California that accuses them of defrauding shareholders by concealing his ties with the suspected Chinese spy.
The lawsuit alleges that the company lied to the media about Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, "who is suspected of seeking to help smuggle Nvidia products to China."
The BBC has contacted Nvidia for comment on the lawsuit.
At the White House, Trump was asked several times when he was made aware of the relationship. He said he was informed "over a period of time" but was not specific.
"I hope there's no problem, I believe he is suffering greatly," the president added.
He said he spoke to Huang on the phone on Monday "just to see if he's feeling alright, how you doing and I asked him about that and he said he absolutely had no idea that the person in question was a spy".
Trump has raised concerns that allowing China to lead in AI would supercharge Beijing's military and surveillance capabilities.
The president added he was "sure" Chinese leader Xi Jinping would "ask me about it" when they next met.
Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?
Huang has admitted that he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.
He said on Monday that he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation the company had launched.
Huang has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week, however it is unclear whether Huang will appear.
A letter said the briefing would be "on Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and your interactions with a publicly reported People's Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang".
Nvidia has declined to comment, while the the BBC has also contacted the committees.
Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond
AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
Some workers the BBC spoke to at Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters on Monday said it was business as usual, despite the intense attention on the company.
Nvidia has been around for decades, with Huang founding it with two other engineers in 1993, but its rise to one of the world's most valuable and powerful companies has only been recent.
It originally designed computer chips for gaming, but its decision to shift focus to AI development turned it into the powerhouse it is today.
Its chips have become so valuable to the AI buildout that the White House previously imposed controls on where its advanced products could be sold.
The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
But Huang has long been against restricting sales to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology.
In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.
Nvidia's most advanced AI semiconductors including the GB200 Blackwell super chip remain blocked from the Chinese market.
Additional reporting by Tessa Wong in Singapore
Why Trump is all-in on AI despite the warnings
What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

articles.title_orig: Oil Prices Extend Decline After Trump Signals Restraint on Iran
articles.title_zh: Oil Prices Extend Decline After Trump Signals Restraint on Iran
articles.content_orig:
President, after talks with Qatari PM, suggests end to war coming ‘fairly soon’ and military escalation not needed
Donald Trump has said that the war in Iran is “effectively over” as he played down concerns that the US would escalate its military campaign against Tehran after the midterm elections.
During a White House press conference, Trump said that Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and that an escalation was not needed.
“At this point, taking the military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing – but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason,” he told reporters during a briefing at the White House.
The remarks followed talks in the Oval Office with the Qatari prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who has lobbied Trump alongside other Gulf countries not to resume the fighting against Iran.
“We’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon,” he added.
Trump has frequently exaggerated claims about the status of negotiations with Iran, saying a final peace deal was imminent dozens of times during the nearly nine-month long war.
The US had continued to move troops to the Middle East in the run-up to the midterm elections. There was speculation that the Trump administration was waiting for the elections to take place before resuming a military campaign, in order to prevent a backlash at the polls.
Republicans were nevertheless routed in a historic defeat in which they lost both houses of Congress, with the vice-president, JD Vance, declaring soon after that the Iran war was a key reason for the defeats.
Trump earlier on Monday said on Truth Social that the leaders of Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait would prefer the “status quo, in other words, a continuation of the Greatest Naval Blockade in History”.
He repeated a mantra that Iran would not be allowed to develop a nuclear weapon, and added that if the situation changed then the US was ready to resume full-scale military action against Iran.
“At this point, however, that seems to be quite unlikely,” he continued. “Israel, and the entire Middle East, are protected from Iranian danger and threats. We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected. At the conclusion of this Military Engagement, the American People, and the World, will be far safer and more secure.”

articles.title_orig: Toyota Sees a U.S. Future for Tiny Trucks With a Devoted Following
articles.title_zh: Toyota Sees a U.S. Future for Tiny Trucks With a Devoted Following
articles.content_orig:
Home > Innovation > Mobility
PLANO, Texas (Nov. 10, 2026) – Yesterday, at simultaneous events in Ypsilanti Township, Michigan, and Frisco, Texas, Toyota Motor North America (TMNA) introduced Scion by Toyota, a new brand built around curiosity, possibility and the freedom to explore mobility in new ways. The company also unveiled the brand’s first vehicle, the KEI-01, an ultra-compact utility truck that will arrive in the U.S. in the second half of 2027.
The company also showcased two additional vehicles—the SxS Concept and the BKE Concept—which represent different expressions of the brand’s vision for future mobility. Together, the three vehicles explore new ideas in utility, adventure, capability and personal expression.
Scion by Toyota is a “freedom lab” built around bold ideas, curiosity and possibility. It starts by asking what’s next—and how far an idea can go. That curiosity is where beyond starts, and opens new possibilities to explore, experiment and make something entirely your own. Scion by Toyota will learn and evolve through new vehicle concepts, designs, capabilities, and experiences that could help shape the future of Toyota mobility.
The brand builds on the experimental spirit associated with the original Scion, reimagined for a new generation. This new endeavor gives Toyota a space to challenge conventions and provide drivers with more freedom to experiment, personalize and create something that is uniquely theirs.
At its heart is the simple idea that there is no single way forward—only the one you choose to make your own. Scion by Toyota explores what becomes possible when mobility supports personal expression, adventure and capability.
“The future of mobility will not be defined by one vehicle, one technology or one way of thinking,” said Simon Humphries, Chief Branding Officer, Head of Design, Toyota Motor Corporation. “Scion by Toyota gives us a place to challenge conventional thinking, explore new possibilities and create mobility in new ways. The KEI-01, SxS and BKE concepts each represent a different possibility—and together, they show what can happen when curiosity leads the way.”
The KEI-01: Where the Journey Begins The KEI-01 is the first manifestation of the Scion by Toyota vision.
Providing the functionality, efficiency and versatility of Japan’s legendary kei trucks, the KEI-01 brings a proven concept to American customers in a packaged way that only Toyota companies can deliver. Designed to meet applicable low-speed vehicle federal safety requirements, the KEI-01 comes standard with a 660cc three-cylinder engine, a continuously variable transmission, and four-wheel drive (4WD) making it an affordable, highly capable, and remarkably maneuverable package.
Toyota has long focused on bringing customers vehicles that fit the way they live and work. For decades, kei trucks have earned a strong reputation in Japan and some other Asian markets for their practicality and versatility. The KEI-01 brings that combination to a new audience while challenging the traditional blueprint, giving customers the freedom to make it their own.
That spirit of going beyond blueprints, combined with Toyota’s commitment to “Fun to Drive,” makes the KEI-01 a natural first expression of the Scion by Toyota brand.
Bringing the KEI-01 to Customers As an intentionally low-volume, niche vehicle, the KEI-01 will initially be offered through a fleet-focused pilot program to help the company learn how it can best serve U.S. customers and use cases. Initial fleet sales are planned through Scion by Toyota dealers selected from current Toyota dealers, which will serve as the customer-facing sales channel. Based on market conditions, customer demand, and operational considerations, Toyota may consider expanding availability to limited retail sales at a later date.
Additional information and the broader sales strategy will be shared as plans are finalized.
Three Vehicles. Three Ways to go Beyond. While the KEI-01 is designed to bring a unique form of utility to U.S. customers, the SxS and BKE concepts demonstrate the broader range of ideas Scion by Toyota is intended to explore.
SxS Concept – Beyond Limits First shown at the 2025 SEMA Show, the SxS Concept is a purpose-built side-by-side concept that reimagines the all-terrain vehicle for a new generation of outdoor enthusiasts. Developed by the company’s North American engineering team, the concept combines a high-output turbocharged four-cylinder hybrid powertrain producing more than 300 horsepower with a compact, purpose-built off-road package.
Designed for everything from spirited desert running to technical rock crawling, the SxS Concept features significant suspension articulation and a nimble footprint. It also features a Silent Mode that allows the vehicle to operate using electric power, offering a different way to experience the outdoors.
Representing Scion by Toyota’s willingness to take Toyota technology and engineering into entirely new spaces, the SxS Concept pushes beyond the limits of terrain, performance and what this kind of vehicle can be. The SxS Concept is more than an exercise in imagination. Toyota will continue advancing the concept, exploring its potential, and evaluating how it could bring an entirely new kind of off-road experience to enthusiasts.
BKE Concept – Beyond Permission The BKE Concept explores another dimension of personal mobility, bringing together compact packaging, utility and adventure in a concept designed to expand the possibilities of how people move through and experience the outdoors.
Where the KEI-01 emphasizes practical utility and the SxS Concept showcases off-road performance, the BKE Concept opens up the space in between—offering freedom to choose your own direction, to take the unexpected turn, and explore beyond permission. Its small, highly adaptable form creates new possibilities for different lifestyles, activities and experiences.
Together, these three distinct vehicles illustrate the breadth of the Scion by Toyota laboratory: from everyday utility, to high-performance adventure, to entirely new forms of personal mobility.
Assembled in America The KEI-01 will be assembled at Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indiana (Toyota Indiana) starting in the second half of 2027, supported by a $34 million investment that will add approximately 50 new jobs.
Assembly at Toyota Indiana represents the company’s continued commitment to investing in the U.S. and American jobs. The investment will establish new vehicle assembly operations and upgrade production and logistics infrastructure, bringing this unique utility vehicle closer to U.S. customers.
Small Footprint. Big Capability. Despite its compact footprint, the KEI-01 delivers capability, versatility and operator comfort. Key highlights include:
Built for Work, Play and Everything in Between The KEI-01 will provide customers with a practical, right-sized solution for buyers who need versatility and durability without the size or expense of a traditional pickup.
The KEI-01 is a right-hand-drive vehicle designed to comply with FMVSS No. 500 requirements for LSVs. Its maximum speed will be 25 miles per hour.
The KEI-01 is designed to meet a wide range of customer needs, including:
Although intentionally small in scale, the KEI-01 delivers impressive cargo capability and excellent maneuverability backed by the company’s reputation for quality, durability and reliability.
Beyond Starts Here Scion by Toyota is more than a return of a familiar name. It is a reinvention of Scion’s experimental spirit around curiosity, possibility and freedom for a new era of mobility.
We’re wired to wonder. What’s next? What’s more? What happens if we try another way? Scion by Toyota starts with those questions—challenging what’s given, pushing past limits and exploring where mobility can take us.
The brand is a freedom lab—a place where ideas can be tested, challenged and evolved, and where something capable from day one can become uniquely

articles.title_orig: The Kraft Group wants to build a $16 billion data center campus in a small Central Mass. town
articles.title_zh: The Kraft Group wants to build a $16 billion data center campus in a small Central Mass. town
articles.content_orig:
Amid a national backlash against data centers, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft’s company is proposing to build one of the largest such facilities in the country, in the central Massachusetts town of Sutton, about 10 miles south of Worcester.
In this rural area, known for its farmland and home to about 9,700 residents, the Kraft Group would build a massive, $16 billion data center campus. The project would include 10 buildings, erected on land currently owned by the Krafts’ Unified Packaging box business. It would push Massachusetts into the world of big data centers, as the fourth-biggest facility in the US, according to the research firm Cleanview.
The proposal must be approved by multiple town committees before moving ahead, and it puts Kraft once again at the center of political controversy , this time as data centers have become political poison across the country . Voters last week from Maine to California approved 44 referendums to block or slow data center construction. Last month, the western Massachusetts community of Westfield moved to block a large data center proposed there.
The Sutton proposal would dwarf the Westfield project. When fully completed in 2033, the Kraft data center would draw 900 megawatts of electricity, enough to power a sizable city.
Given the political winds blowing against data center construction, the Kraft Group is likely to face strong local opposition. Residents have already been stirring in comments on the town Facebook group.
“There’s been a pretty quick response from the community expressing concerns,” said state Rep. Joe McKenna, who represents the area. The main issues are that the project could drive up electricity rates, consume too much water, and generate noise, he said. “They’re concerns that I share, but I’m also not willing to say ‘No’ just based on a fear of an unknown, or fear of an uncertainty,” McKenna added.
Sutton’s Town Manager, Austin J. Cyganiewicz, confirmed the $16 billion proposal from the Kraft Group and Unified Global Packaging Group in a letter sent Monday to the town’s Select Board. The board is slated to meet Tuesday evening.
The Krafts clashed last summer with Foxborough town officials amid World Cup talks, battling over $8 million in security costs. And in September, Robert Kraft drew wide criticism for barring rap artist Macklemore from performing at Gillette Stadium over his remarks in support of Palestinians.
As for the move into data centers, Massachusetts has so far not been an appealing destination for the large, energy-hungry facilities powering the AI boom — Sutton would be the first. That’s because the state has among the highest electricity rates in the country, not to mention high land prices and construction costs, IDC analyst Matt Eastwood said.
But as the AI boom moves from early development to broader usage, every part of the country will need local, large data centers, according to Eastwood.
If approved, the first two buildings at the Sutton site, off Boston and Providence roads, would open in 2029, and two more facilities would come online each year through 2033, for a total of 10.
The Kraft Group did not yet provide information about possible tenants of the data center. But they’re making a bet based based on the plans of AI giants like OpenAI and Anthropic, which are expected to spend hundreds of billions of dollars leasing space in such facilities.
Given the forecasts of exploding AI usage, businesses eventually will need nearby data centers to avoid software slowdowns, Eastwood said. “You’ll end up with an AI infrastructure that’s much more distributed and not as centralized,” he said, with a handful of mega-sized data centers needed in New England.
In parts of the country with numerous data centers, the facilities appear to have driven up electricity rates . The Sutton campus, if fully built out, would draw roughly 900 megawatts of power and at $16 billion would represent a multiple of the $2.8 billion in assessed value of all the property in Sutton, Cyganiewicz wrote.
The power draw would equal about 7 percent of the state’s peak power usage on the hottest summer day last year, of about 12,575 megawatts.
For the town of Sutton, which is struggling to balance its budget over the next few years, property tax revenue from the data center could win over skeptics.
The first two buildings on the data center campus would pay $10.4 million annually in property taxes starting in fiscal year 2031. That sum would rise to about $27.8 million a year on all 10 buildings in 2035, Cyganiewicz estimated in his letter.
In a town with a $40 million annual budget, that would be a huge windfall, potentially cutting property tax bills for residents by thousands of dollars. An average single-family homeowner in 2031 could see their tax bill fall to $6,846 from $9,134, according to Cyganiewicz.
Still, “the proposal is tentative,” he wrote. “No application has been filed, and important details on power, water, equipment and site impacts are still to come.”
The Kraft Group did not return a request for comment Tuesday.
None of the town board members immediately responded to requests for comment on the proposal, which was previously reported by MassLive.
Data centers have become increasingly controversial as critics point to their environmental impacts, energy consumption, and broader concerns about the effect of artificial intelligence on the job market. Governor Maura Healey in September signed an executive order to block new data centers in Massachusetts unless they get local approval.
Rep. Jim McGovern, whose Congressional district includes Sutton, has been a leading opponent of data centers and cosponsored a bill to impose a national moratorium. But McGovern said it would be up to residents to decide whether to move forward with the Kraft proposal.
“Costs of utilities have gone up for a lot of people because the data centers eat up a lot of energy and take a lot of water... so for me, I don’t like them,” he said. “But, ultimately, it’s up to the people of Sutton.”
Nearly across the board during the midterms, pro-data center candidates backed by Big Tech, including Senate candidates Jon Husted in Ohio and Ken Paxton in Texas, lost.
Many House candidates supporting AI and data centers came up short, too, including Derrick Van Orden in Wisconsin and Rob Bresnahan in Pennsylvania. And in dozens of local referendums around the country, from Wells, Maine, to Defiance, Ohio, and Emporia, Kansas, voters approved bans or restrictions on data centers.
Jim Puzzanghera of the Globe staff contributed reporting.
This is a developing story and will be updated.
Travis Andersen can be reached at travis.andersen@globe.com . Aaron Pressman can be reached at aaron.pressman@globe.com . Follow him @ampressman .

articles.title_orig: Despite Denial, Trump Was Told on Trip to China About Spying on Nvidia Leader
articles.title_zh: Despite Denial, Trump Was Told on Trip to China About Spying on Nvidia Leader
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia has announced an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang.
President Donald Trump said the head of Nvidia told him in a phone call on Monday that he "didn't know" he was involved with an alleged Chinese spy.
Trump's comments come a day after the tech giant announced an investigation into Jensen Huang following reporting that the Nvidia CEO had an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, identified as Alice Huang, a top executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed.
Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about it.
"He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy," the president told reporters during a press briefing.
"I asked him that question -- 'Did you have any idea that she was a spy?' He said, 'I had no idea that she was a spy,' and I really believe him," Trump continued.
Trump dodged multiple questions about when he was first briefed on the matter. At one point, the president said the FBI is investigating.
"I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape," Trump said, without elaborating.
Trump's comments came the same day a lawsuit seeking class action status was filed in federal court against Nvidia and Jensen Huang, alleging that the company "made false and misleading statements" regarding the CEO's interactions with Alice Huang. The complaint was filed on behalf of an Nvidia shareholder.
On Sunday, Nvidia said that its board launched an independent investigation "in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."
The statement added that a "committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."
Huang "fully supports the review" and will cooperate with it, the Nvidia statement further said.
"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," according to the statement.
"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," the statement further said.
"The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team," according to the statement.
The New York Times reported late last month that Huang, who runs the world's largest computer chip manufacturer, was targeted by a Chinese espionage plot centered around a woman they identified as Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence officials determined was funneling information to Beijing and had developed a "close relationship" with Jensen Huang.
The Chinese government has denied the allegations, calling them "baseless and purely slanderous smears against China."
Neither Alice Huang nor her employer, Megaspeed International, responded to ABC News' request for comment after the New York Times story broke.
"Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected" and are part of Jensen Huang's job, an Nvidia spokesperson told ABC News at the time.
However, Nvidia on Sunday shared with ABC News an internal message Jensen Huang sent to employees, in which he said he was "unfaithful" to his wife.
"My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," the message said, in part. It did not name Alice Huang nor any other person.
Addressing Nvidia staff, partners and shareholders, Huang went on to say, "my responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."
"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," Huang's message said.
Following the New York Times report, congressional Republicans on the Select Committee on China sent a letter to Jensen Huang requesting that he appear for a closed-door briefing Nov. 18 concerning his relationship with Alice Huang.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the letter said, in part. It is not known if Huang will appear before the committee.
"Today's news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption," an NVIDIA spokesperson told ABC News Sunday.

articles.title_orig: Google warns users to protect their inbox as new hacking tool threatens to expose your private information
articles.title_zh: Google warns users to protect their inbox as new hacking tool threatens to expose your private information
articles.content_orig:
Changing your passwords is no longer enough to avoid this new cyberattack tool.
Gmail users should review their account security settings following reports of a new cybercrime tool designed to target private email inboxes.
The software, known as Remus Stealer, has been advertised on online forums as a tool that allows hackers to get their hands on unauthorized access to people’s personal emails, according to Hudson Rock , a cybersecurity company that investigated Remus Stealer.
The operators of the Remus Stealer malware are marketing a new capability that allows criminals to access victims’ Gmail inboxes directly from a control panel, according to insights from Cyber Insider. The developers of the software claim that cybercriminals can maintain access to messages even after users change their Google passwords or close their web browsers.
According to Hudson Rock, Remus Stealer says criminals who subscribe to their service — for $1,000 a month — will get access to private Gmail inboxes.
Infostealer malware is designed to collect sensitive data, such as passwords and login credentials, from infected devices. These infections typically occur through downloads, disguised as legitimate software, although the exact method Remus uses has not been confirmed.
Hudson Rock examined the version 1.3.9 announcement, contacted the developer, and spoke with a person who publicly endorsed the feature to learn more about the hacking software.
A user of Remus reported to Hudson Rock that compromised email access persisted for the hacker even after the user closed their browser and updated their account password.
The source also told Hudson Rock that verification codes from third-party online services could be intercepted through the application. Remus promotes email-code interception without collecting browser cookie files, claims that password changes and session revocation do not stop it, and advertises shareable mailbox links.
However, researchers have not independently verified whether ongoing message collection continues after an account is fully secured and active sessions are revoked.
Other online accounts may also be vulnerable , as unauthorized email access can allow individuals to receive password reset links and verification codes.
For the $1,000 monthly fee, hackers have a central dashboard to view email data and share access with other hackers.
Cybersecurity researchers at Hudson Rock reviewed promotional materials for the tool and noted that while updating passwords is a necessary precaution, additional security steps should be taken.
Images of the user interface show options to search email contents, sender details, and timestamps, indicating access to complete mailboxes rather than single codes.
Google recommends that users update their passwords and terminate unrecognized sessions. “Users can invalidate stolen sessions by removing malware from the affected device and revoking active sessions,” a Google spokesperson told Cybernews
Researchers advise users to review account settings, including forwarding rules, filters, recovery options, and third-party app permissions, to ensure no unauthorized changes have occurred.
The Post reached out to Hudson Rock and they did not immediately reply for comment.

articles.title_orig: Germany news: Presidential candidate Ilse Aigner meets with parties in Bundestag, but not AfD or Linke
articles.title_zh: Germany news: Presidential candidate Ilse Aigner meets with parties in Bundestag, but not AfD or Linke
articles.content_orig:
This blog is now closed. Read below for a roundup of headlines and analysis from Germany on Tuesday, November 10, 2026:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar pledged to strengthen relations between their countries during talks in Berlin, announcing plans for closer cooperation on energy, defense and trade.
Merz described the meeting, attended by several ministers from both governments, as part of a fresh start in relations between Germany and Hungary.
"The German and Hungarian histories are closely intertwined," Merz said, adding that he wanted to use the momentum of Hungary's new government to revive bilateral ties.
Magyar highlighted the significance of his visit taking place around November 9 —the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989.
"It is a very important day in the life of the German people," Magyar said, adding that Hungary was proud of the role it had played in those historic events .
In August 1989, hundreds of East Germans escaped to Austria during the Pan-European Picnic on the Hungarian border. Hungary subsequently opened its border to East German refugees in September, allowing tens of thousands to flee to the West and helping accelerate the collapse of communist rule in East Germany.
Turning to economic relations, Merz said Germany was Hungary's largest trading partner and welcomed what he called positive signals from Budapest about improving conditions for German companies.
Merz also offered to help Hungary reduce its dependence on Russian energy imports by providing access to capacity at German liquefied natural gas terminals and sharing expertise in renewable energy.
"The stars are very favorable," Magyar said, referring to prospects for strengthening the countries' already close economic and cultural ties.
Magyar welcomed the offer but stressed that prices would be crucial.
Ilse Aigner is highly likely to become Germany's first female president after securing support from the governing conservatives and Social Democrats (SPD) , alongside a recommendation from the Green Party leadership.
The governing parties already hold an estimated majority of around 50 votes in the Federal Convention, which elects the president. Green backing would substantially widen that margin, making a first-round victory on January 30 highly likely.
Aigner, Bavaria 's state parliament president from the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU) , received standing ovations from lawmakers of her party and its sister party, the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) .
The SPD, which has formally endorsed her, also welcomed her with applause.
But Aigner's decision to decline an invitation from the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) prompted criticism from co-leader Alice Weidel .
"Apparently, we cannot expect political impartiality from Ilse Aigner," Weidel said.
Aigner's team cited AfD lawmaker Beatrix von Storch's disparaging response to her nomination as the reason for declining. Aigner herself did not address the dispute during her press statement.
The Federal Convention comprises Bundestag lawmakers and an equal number of delegates chosen by state parliaments. It will elect a successor to President Frank-Walter Steinmeier .
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Germany's conservative presidential candidate Ilse Aigner has highlighted various ways she would break new ground if elected as the country's first female president.
Aigner was nominated to succeed President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in the January 30 election.
She presented herself to parliamentary groups and highlighted her route into politics through an apprenticeship and technical work rather than university as one difference from predecessors.
Aigner would also be the first president from Bavaria's conservative Christian Social Union (CSU).
"In many ways, I am something of a first — or could be," the Bavarian state parliament president said. "And I'm also single — I always mention that too."
Defending democracy would be her central priority, she said during an appearance with Chancellor Friedrich Merz and CSU leader Markus Söder.
"I want to stand up for democracy — for me, that really is a mission," Aigner said, warning that democracy was under pressure "from within and from outside."
She pledged to build bridges, overcome divisions and remain close to ordinary people. "I will be one of them," she said.
The top candidate to replace Frank-Walter Steinmeier as Germany's president, Ilse Aigner , is set to visit the Bundestag, where she will meet with the center-right CDU/CSU bloc, the Social Democrats and the Greens.
She has said she will not meet with the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) after one of their top members called her nomination a "disgrace." She also has not received an official invitation from the Left party.
Aigner was officially nominated by the CDU/CSU bloc , also known as the Union, on Monday, practically securing her future as German president. She already has support from the SPD and Greens.
The official vote will take place on January 30. The president is chosen by the Bundestag. Despite being the highest political office in the country, it is a largely ceremonial role.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Three left-leaning parties are seeking to form a coalition government for the north-eastern state to block the far-right AfD, which won the most votes in the September election, from governing the state.
SPD state premier candidate Manuela Schwesig said the agreement followed "intensive negotiations, often late into the night."
The agreement consists of a 133-page coalition program with the title "Solidarity, Confidence, Future" ( Zusammenhalt, Zuversicht, Zukunft ).
The so-called Red-Red-Green coalition will be voted on by the parties' membership on Friday and Saturday, with Schwesig expecting to be voted in as state premier on Monday.
The district court in Rostock, in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania , has found a 30-year-old woman guilty of the murder of an 8-year-old boy and sentenced her to life in prison.
Gina H. had been in a relationship with the boy's father and saw the child as an obstacle to the continued relationship with the man.
According to the prosecution, in October 2025, the accused lured the boy to a nearby pond where she stabbed him to death. She then tried to burn the body to cover up the crime.
It was, in fact, Gina H. who notified police of the body after first claiming to have come across it while walking the dog. She has consistently pleaded not guilty to the crime.
Prosecutors said that despite ending the relationship ending in August last year, the defendant and the boy's father were again in a relationship, with him caring for her horses while she was in pre-trial detention.
The story garnered national attention and sparked outrage when it first broke. Long queues had formed in front of the court ahead of Tuesday's sentencing.
Following earlier reports of a shooting in Hamburg 's HafenCity, police have now reported that the 68-year-old suspect shot himself in a hotel room.
"There are indications that the circumstances surrounding the crime may be related to family matters. Our homicide division has been notified and is taking over the investigation," police said on WhatsApp.
Police in southern Germany are now looking into whether the shooting in Hamburg has some connection with two bodies that were found on Tuesday morning in the town of Eningen unter Achalm, to the south of Stuttgart.
Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
articles.title_zh: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate the affair between its chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy.
Jensen Huang, a co-founder of Nvidia who has led it to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman outside of his marriage.
The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing. She was an executive at a Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia.
Nvidia said on Tuesday that Wachtell attorney Joon Kim was set to lead "a thorough and independent investigation" into Jensen Huang's affair. The FBI is also conducting its own probe.
Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the US artificial intelligence (AI) boom given it is the sole manufacturer of a crucial computer chip required for successfully operating AI tools.
Shares in the company fell to a near-yearly low on Tuesday, wiping more than $500bn (£375bn) off Nvidia's stock market value since Friday, even as tech stocks have recovered since last week's sell-off.
Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive of an Nvidia customer, who is also believed by the US government to be spying for China, has business and national security implications.
Megaspeed had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked.
Nvidia has also maintained the US government did not inform the firm that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern.
According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington in spring of this year warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Beijing has rejected claims that Jensen Huang has been targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "intended to smear and malign China".
US President Donald Trump said Monday that he had spoken to Jensen Huang and that the Nvidia boss told him "I had no idea she was a spy." Trump said he believed the him.
However, the relationship has drawn more political attention. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Jensen Huang to appear next week for a closed door briefing.
The Nvidia boss has yet to say whether he will attend, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC.
The committee has the authority to subpoena Jensen Huang, effectively forcing him to appear before the committee, if deemed necessary.
When announcing on Sunday that it would investigate the affair, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.
It added that a committee of independent directors would oversee the probe.
Joon Kim, who will lead Nvidia's investigation, is a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District and spent several years working as a government attorney focused on fraud and other criminal acts.
Wachtell is one of the largest law firms in the US and has several notable clients in the tech industry. Among them are OpenAI and Salesforce.
The investigation will likely be treated as urgent, according to sources familiar with the matter, as Jensen Huang's public image is tightly intertwined with Nvidia.
He has become a key public figure in the development on AI, arguing the technology is a "new industrial revolution" and is on par with the advent of electricity.
It is unclear, however, if Wachtell will be able to interview Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang.
A spokesperson for Nvidia declined to comment on Tuesday when asked if Jensen Huang had retained any additional of his own legal representation amid the company investigation and the separate one launched by the FBI.

articles.title_orig: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO
articles.title_zh: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO
articles.content_orig:
As Anthropic barrels toward an enormous IPO that could value it at $1.4 trillion, the company has disclosed a tidbit in its new S-1 filing about how many shares each of its seven co-founders plan to sell.
Each will sell 3,378,378 shares. Anthropic has floated an unusually broad initial price range of $70 to $78 a share. At the midrange of $74, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million.
At the low end, $70, each would have to settle for pocketing just over $236 million in cash; at the high end, $78, each would take in just under $264 million.
However, in an IPO as eagerly anticipated as this one, companies can often price shares above the initial range.
The S-1 is already hinting at high demand. Board member Reed Hastings has indicated he wants to buy $300 million worth of shares through his donor-advised fund. Board member Christopher Liddell also wants to buy $3 million worth of shares.
The seven co-founders are Dario Amodei, CEO; Daniela Amodei, president and chair of the board; Tom Brown, chief compute officer; Jack Clark, head of public benefit; Jared Kaplan, chief science officer (pictured above); Sam McCandlish, chief architect; and Christopher Olah, interpretability research lead.
After the sale, each of them will own about 3.2% of the total outstanding Class A shares, the S-1 says, or roughly 22% collectively. That’s not their share of the company overall. Class A is just one of Anthropic’s share classes, and other holders, including Amazon and Google, hold nonvoting Class N shares, so the founders’ stake in the company’s total equity will be considerably smaller. Even still, they, as a group, remain in control of the company. Each will also receive one share of Class F stock, which carries supervoting rights. Collectively, the founders will control 51.1% of the votes, but no single founder will hold significantly more shares or votes than the others.
As is now industry lore, the seven left OpenAI to start Anthropic in 2021 after disagreements with OpenAI’s leadership over how AI should be built. Siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, who held senior research and policy roles at OpenAI, were joined by five fellow OpenAI colleagues in forming a company that has said, very publicly and from the start, that it’s more focused on AI safety than its rivals, including the founders’ former employer.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday that he would stress the importance of “non-interference in our affairs by China” when he meets President Xi Jinping later this month.
A 2025 public inquiry into allegations of election meddling identified China as “the most active perpetrator of foreign interference targeting Canada’s democratic institutions”.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia CEO Huang Gets More Bad News. Cathie Wood Keeps the Faith.
articles.title_zh: Nvidia CEO Huang Gets More Bad News. Cathie Wood Keeps the Faith.
articles.content_orig:
Democratic leader Sen. Charles Schumer ripped President Donald Trump on Tuesday for defending embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the expense of U.S. national security.
"The press reports that Trump was briefed more than a year ago that Nvidia's CEO was having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and Trump didn't do anything – anything – about it," Schumer, D-N.Y., said on the Senate floor.
"Can you believe that?" said Schumer, the Senate's minority leader.
Schumer's broadside came on the heels of New York Times reports that Trump had been briefed about Huang's extramarital affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang — whom U.S. intelligence concluded was a spy for China — and opted not to do anything about it.
Trump suggested to reporters on Monday that he only recently learned of the allegations about Alice Huang, and the president commented Monday that he "really" believes Jensen Huang's claim to him directly that he had no idea Alice Huang was a spy.
"One of our most important companies that is involved in national security, and the CEO might be having an affair with a Chinese spy, and Trump did nothing about it," Schumer said Tuesday.
"What a dereliction of duty. He's supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends," Schumer said. "Trump has been busy trying to defend Jensen Huang when he ought to be defending our national security. It's that simple, it's obvious."
Schumer's comments escalated growing bipartisan concern in Congress about the Nvidia CEO, whose company makes advanced chips that power artificial intelligence in the U.S. and China's race to dominate that technology.
Schumer noted that Trump earlier this year invited Huang to join him on a state visit to Beijing, and that he took Huang's advice by granting the People's Republic of China "access to some of our most advanced AI chips."
Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump's controversial White House ballroom project, the Democrat said.
"Despite talking a big game, Trump continues to show a troubling resistance to confront China on AI and to protect American national security," Schumer said. "I've been saying it for years: our cutting-edge AI chips are too valuable to fall into the hands of potential adversaries."
Schumer in his speech called on Republicans to join Democrats in passing several pieces of legislation — the AI OVERWATCH Act, the MATCH Act, and the Chip Security Act — which he said would "cut off China's access to advanced American technology."
"We also need answers on Nvidia's influence campaign and how [it] affected the Trump administration's national security decisions, including the loosening – the loosening – of key export controls," Schumer said. "We need a full accounting for Trump's failure to address foreign espionage in the American tech industry."
CNBC has requested comment from the White House about Schumer's remarks.
The remarks came nearly a week after Democrats won enough Senate and House races nationwide to take majority control of both chambers in January. Schumer hopes to be selected majority leader.
Regardless of which Democrats are tapped to serve as majority leaders in both chambers, the party will have the ability to launch investigations into Nvidia and Huang.
Earlier Tuesday, Rep. John Moolenaar , R-Mich., said on CNBC's " Squawk Box " that Congress needs to "get to the bottom" of Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.
Moolenaar, who chairs the House Permanent Select Committee on China, said he wants to know whether Huang shared privileged information with a Chinese spy; whether Huang was influenced to lobby against preventing chip sales to China; and whether China was given preference in purchasing Nvidia's limited supply of advanced chips.
And he urged a thorough internal investigation of Huang.
"If it becomes less of an investigation, more of damage control, that's not going to work because people have to have confidence," Moolenaar said.
"We're dealing with the country, the Chinese Communist Party that is a foremost adversary, that's funding wars and supporting Russia, supporting Iran, North Korea," he said. "And we have basically a Cold War race with technology. We cannot allow the premier company at the forefront of this to, in some way, be irresponsible."
Congressional scrutiny of Huang's affair has intensified since members returned to Washington on Monday, a day after Nvidia announced it was opening an independent investigation of Jensen Huang's conduct.
Rep. Jay Obernolte, R-Calif., co-chair of the House AI task force, raised concerns that the scandal could plague talks over export controls for advanced AI chips. "It's important not to have a personal scandal interfere with the substantive policy discussion about to what degree we should be allowing the export of cutting edge chips to our geopolitical competitors like China," Obernolte told CNBC. "I hope this isn't a distraction because that's a very important conversation that needs to happen."
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries , D-N.Y., said in a press conference on Monday that "we're going to need a full briefing specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened and what the implications are in terms of national security"
Moolenaar co-authored a letter with Florida Rep. Brian Mast and Arkansas Rep. Rick Crawford on Nov. 5 asking Huang to appear before the Select Committee on China, the House Foreign Affairs Committee and House Select Committee on Intelligence. Mast chairs the foreign affairs panel, and Crawford chairs intelligence.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the three Republicans wrote.
Mast said Tuesday he did not know whether Huang had responded to the letter he authored with Moolenar and Crawford demanding the tech CEO brief them. "I can't say that I've heard an answer back yet that," Mast told reporters at the Capitol. Mast then rattled off a list of questions he has for Huang, including where the company has been selling chips, what Megaspeed may have been using them for, who has been remotely accessing Nvidia chips and what information was passed between Huang and the potential spy. "Obviously questions relating to his relationship and what information was or was not passed about anything," Mast said when asked what he wants answered.
Mast said he "can't say it would hurt" to hear from the Commerce Department as well, noting he speaks regularly to the Bureau of Industry and Security. "So that's obviously something that falls directly under Commerce," he said

articles.title_orig: Russia and Ukraine begin U.S.-backed peace talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.title_zh: Russia and Ukraine begin U.S.-backed peace talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.content_orig:
krainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday that fresh U.S.-brokered peace talks with Russia were "constructive and quite substantive," offering an encouraging assessment of renewed diplomatic efforts by President Donald Trump's administration to end the war.
The roughly four-hour negotiations in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates, marked the first direct trilateral discussions involving Washington, Moscow and Kyiv since February, with representatives agreeing to continue talks Wednesday, Reuters reported.
Zelenskyy specifically identified three areas of substantive discussion: humanitarian measures and prisoner exchanges, long-term security guarantees intended to prevent another Russian invasion, and possible steps toward reducing hostilities.
Although he characterized the discussions positively, Zelenskyy did not announce any agreements or specify whether the sides had narrowed their differences on the central disputes standing in the way of a peace settlement.
"The release of prisoners is a priority," Zelenskyy wrote on X following a briefing from his negotiating team.
"They spoke in detail about the substance of security guarantees for Ukraine and the foundations for ensuring these guarantees function over the long term," he added.
"Real tools are needed to block any recurrence of the war."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Paris, also offered an encouraging assessment, describing the negotiations as "very productive," according to The Associated Press.
But Rubio cautioned that substantial work remained before an agreement could be reached.
Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff represented Washington in the negotiations, following weeks of preparatory discussions with Russian and Ukrainian officials.
Kushner previously said those contacts had narrowed differences between the two countries, although he did not specify which issues had moved closer to resolution, according to the New York Post.
The Ukrainian delegation was led by Rustem Umerov, head of the country's Foreign Intelligence Service, while Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky headed Moscow's team.
Neither Zelenskyy nor Russian President Vladimir Putin attended.
Despite the positive assessments, major obstacles remain, particularly over territory occupied by Russian forces since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Russia controls approximately one-fifth of Ukraine and demands that Kyiv surrender the remaining Ukrainian-held territory in the eastern Donbas region.
Moscow also wants Ukraine to abandon its NATO ambitions and accept restrictions on its military.
Zelenskyy has rejected those demands, arguing that territorial concessions and military limitations could leave Ukraine vulnerable to another Russian invasion.
According to Reuters, U.S. negotiators believe Zelenskyy and Putin might eventually accept a territorial compromise, although a senior Ukrainian official disputed suggestions that Kyiv would consider such concessions.
Another major disagreement concerns the sequence of steps toward peace.
Ukraine wants an immediate ceasefire followed by negotiations on a comprehensive settlement, while Russia insists that broader security arrangements must be addressed first.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov reiterated Moscow's position Tuesday, arguing that a comprehensive European security framework should precede a settlement of the Ukraine conflict, Reuters reported.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has taken the opposite position, saying broader security negotiations should follow a ceasefire.
European governments also want a greater role in shaping any agreement affecting the continent's security.
Rubio said Washington hopes eventually to expand the trilateral negotiations to include European representatives.
The diplomatic initiative comes amid continuing hostilities, with Russian forces striking Ukrainian energy infrastructure as winter approaches.
Overnight attacks hit 10 Ukrainian regions and five major electrical substations, causing power outages and killing two people, Reuters reported.
Ukraine has meanwhile intensified drone attacks against Russian oil refineries and other infrastructure.
Trump expressed optimism Monday, saying Washington was seeing a "very strong inclination" toward ending the war because both countries were exhausted by the fighting.
Zelenskyy said he had instructed his delegation to continue negotiations Wednesday and pursue further discussions with American and European officials in the coming days.

articles.title_orig: PS Plus Pulls Plug on PC Streaming After Fewer Than 1% Used It
articles.title_zh: PS Plus Pulls Plug on PC Streaming After Fewer Than 1% Used It
articles.content_orig:
Sony will kill the ability to stream PlayStation games on the PC beginning 10th December, with the platform holder stating fewer than 0.4% of eligible PS Plus Premium subscribers used it.
Members of the manufacturer’s most expensive tier can currently stream and play titles from the PS Plus Premium catalogue using a PC app, which will be discontinued next month.
Curiously, this service has always been limited to PS4 and PS3 titles – it never expanded support to the PS5 library.
The pages on PlayStation.com where you used to be able to download the software have already been removed in anticipation.
Writing on the PS Blog , Sony’s Adam Michel said:
“PlayStation believes in providing high-quality experiences to our players, and we regularly review offerings to ensure we are focusing on experiences our members value most. With a very small number of eligible PS Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PS Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PS Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available.”
Once upon a time, I did temporarily use PS Now streaming on my laptop when I went through a period where I didn’t have access to my consoles. But I haven’t used the feature since.
I don’t think Sony promoted this particularly prominently, so I expect many fans may only be finding out about it now.
But I think this is probably part of a broader push by the Japanese giant to move its software off PC. Internally, it’s pivoted away from porting its first-party single player games to the platform. Now it’s ceasing streaming as well.
It should be stressed that PS Plus Premium cloud streaming will remain available on the PS5, PS4, and PS Portal. There will also be no changes to Remote Play functionality.
Will you be affected by this at all? Given the numbers touted in Sony’s article, I can’t imagine many of you will have used this.

articles.title_orig: In Argentina, Pope Leo Walks in the Giant Shadow of Francis
articles.title_zh: In Argentina, Pope Leo Walks in the Giant Shadow of Francis
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV met with bishops, priests, deacons, religious, seminarians and pastoral workers at the Cathedral of Our Lady of the Assumption in Córdoba on Tuesday, the third day of his apostolic visit to Argentina.
The encounter included a welcome address by Cardinal Ángel Sixto Rossi, in which he called for a Church attentive to peopleâs needs, particularly those most wounded, and committed to walking alongside them in neighbourhoods, prisons and hospitals, as well as testimonies from four people involved in the life of the Church.
In his address, the Pope invited those present to return to the source of their vocation and renew their relationship with Christ, recalling the spiritual tradition of Argentina and figures such as Mama Antula, Saint José Gabriel del Rosario Brochero and Pope Francis.
Drawing on the Ignatian Spiritual Exercises, he asked them to consider the question: âWhy are we here?â He warned that pastoral commitments can sometimes take the place of prayer and intimacy with God.
âWe work hard for God yet spend less and less time with him,â he said, calling for renewed attention to the Eucharist, the Word of God and personal prayer.
Pope Leo also highlighted the need for ongoing conversion, humility and freedom to respond to God's call, including when it leads in unexpected directions. He encouraged pastoral workers to examine their lives and remain open to the places and people to whom they are sent.
Reflecting on the Church's social mission, he recognised its commitment to those who suffer, while insisting that material assistance must be accompanied by spiritual care and the proclamation of Christ.
Again, he recalled Pope Francis and his teaching, and he quoted Evangelii Gaudium : âthe worst discrimination which the poor suffer is the lack of spiritual care.â
The Church, the Pope added, is not simply a humanitarian organisation, but is sent to bring Christ to the world.
Addressing seminarians, Pope Leo encouraged them to learn to see others through God's eyes and to allow themselves to be evangelised by the people they encounter. âEven those who have the least can teach us a great deal,â he said, referring to the testimony shared during the meeting.
He also spoke of perseverance when ministry brings weariness or few visible results. âEven amid doubts and weariness, one continues to say with oneâs life: âHere I am,ââ he said.
And recalling Saint Héctor Valdivielso Sáez and Saint Brochero, he explained that physical limitations and difficult circumstances need not bring an end to service.
Responding to the testimonies brought by Laura Sampallo, a consecrated woman, and by Father Martín Carranza, a priest of the Archdiocese of Córdoba, the Pope recalled his own recent hospitalisation and encouraged those present not to lose their missionary zeal.
âOur strength may run out, but Godâs power never will,â he said, adding that technology can also help the Church continue to proclaim the Gospel.
Bringing his address to a close, Pope Leo returned to the Ignatian prayer of offering oneself to God: âTake, Lord, and receiveâ¦â He invited those present to ask whether the Lord could still make use of them. âIf the answer remains âyes,â then there is much ahead of us. Let us not give up!â
Finally, he encouraged the Church in Argentina to continue fostering vocations, vibrant parishes, religious communities and seminaries capable of forming people for holiness. He also recalled Pope Francisâ appeal to young people in Rio de Janeiro, in which he spoke of a Church that continues to âmake noiseâ through its missionary presence.
Pope Leo concluded by entrusting the Church in Argentina to Our Lady of Luján and urging those present to return to their communities with renewed hope, freedom, and commitment to their mission.
